provenance.policy: Reviewed prose and execution guidance only. Original executable sources remain the sole algorithm owners.

guidance.svelte: Use an isolated Svelte 5 project. Copy all supplied companion files together; the built-in DOM/store preview does not compile App.svelte. Compile .svelte components and workspace.svelte.js with the appropriate Svelte compiler entry points, then verify interactions and cleanup in a browser.
guidance.typescript: Run tsc against the supplied lesson.ts with strict checking, no emit, and ES2023/DOM libraries. Preserve @ts-expect-error directives; an unused directive is a failed fixture check. Typechecking does not execute DOM interactions.
guidance.html: Serve the complete lesson folder over local HTTP. Keep original lang and srclang fixture values, asset URLs and script ordering inputs unchanged. Verify playback/captions, sandbox behavior, or parsing order in the browser as directed by README.en.md.
guidance.wat: Compile kernel.wat in an isolated copy with WABT, then run the real Node assertion harness. Existing legacy kernel.wasm can run directly with Node. The iframe preview does not execute Wasm or certify these checks.
guidance.playwright: Run the supplied spec and fixture in an isolated Playwright project. The generated config starts its own HTTP fixture server. Run lessons sequentially on port 4179, pin the browser and environment, and review visual baselines before treating screenshot checks as verified.
guidance.scene: Use the existing React/Three host and scene-container dimensions. Preserve SceneLab.tsx and createScene.ts relative imports. Verify rotation pause/resume, camera reset, resizing, unmount and resource disposal in a WebGL-capable browser. Typechecking does not certify GPU rendering.
guidance.r3f: Use an isolated React/Vite host with React, @react-three/fiber and three. Copy App.jsx and provide your own valid public/model.glb; this repository does not supply that model. Test loading, Suspense, ErrorBoundary, and the missing.glb path in a WebGL-capable browser. A bundle check does not certify model loading or GPU correctness.

# Media, captions, and failure paths

Run `python -m http.server 8000` in this folder, then open http://localhost:8000/index.html . Captions may be restricted when opened with file:// .

1. Play the 6-second silent sample.mp4 and select Korean in the captions menu. Blue changes to orange at 3 seconds.
2. Use the missing-file button to check the 404 and transcript fallback. Also test restoring the valid file.
3. Change the timing and text in captions.vtt, reload, and compare.

This silent synthetic video is not intended to assess caption quality for actual speech. When replacing it with a speech video you own, update both captions and transcript.

The playback asset was generated with the FFmpeg color source. No external video or audio was used. See the generate-foundations-examples.mjs comments in the repository for the generation command.
documents.src/labs/html-step-21/README.en.md:
# iframe sandbox boundary

Run `python -m http.server 8000` in this folder, then open http://localhost:8000/index.html .

- Unchecked: sandbox="". The guide HTML is visible, but script, button handlers, and postMessage do not run.
- Checked: sandbox="allow-scripts". The same document reloads, and the counter and messaging work. The origin is "null" because allow-same-origin is absent.
- The parent page checks event.source and the message type. This example does not send confidential data.

Frontory also applies a parent CSP restriction, so perform this comparison on a standalone local server. Do not add allow-same-origin. Record blocked requests and console messages alongside actual button behavior.
documents.src/labs/html-step-23/README.en.md:
# Classic, defer, and async loading

Run `python -m http.server 8000` in this folder, then open http://localhost:8000/index.html . The two external scripts are intentionally placed in head before target.

1. Default defer: body inline → first.js → second.js → DOMContentLoaded. Both external scripts report targetExists:true.
2. Remove both defer attributes: first.js → second.js → body inline. Both external scripts block parsing, so targetExists:false.
3. Change both defer attributes to async: scripts run in download-completion order. Record DOM availability and execution order each time. Do not assume async always changes the order or always executes before the DOM exists.
4. Enable Disable cache and slow network conditions in DevTools Network, then retry. If the small local files show no difference, record that observation.

Times are observations from performance.now. The console and page display the same loadingLog. This performs actual fetch and parsing; distinguish it from the static source checks inside Frontory.

# Svelte component lab

`example.js` demonstrates an actual Svelte writable store and DOM adapter in the built-in runner. It is not a Svelte component.

In a Svelte 5 Vite project, replace `src/App.svelte` with this folder’s `App.svelte` and copy `PointerCanvas.svelte` to the same location. Run the project’s development server. Manage the external project’s packages and lockfile separately.

Repeatedly hide/show the component and change the period. The cleanup returned by `onMount` removes the timer and pointer listener. `#key period` creates a new component when the period changes. No Canvas timer should remain while it is hidden.
documents.src/labs/svelte-03/README.en.md:
# Compare identical requirements

The built-in examples use actual React, Vue, and Svelte stores, but the Svelte column uses a handwritten DOM adapter. Do not compare that column’s DOM code size with Svelte component code size.

Replace `src/App.svelte` in a Svelte 5 Vite project with the supplied file to run the actual component. On the same three cards, repeat: complete card 1 → enable the incomplete filter → disable the filter. Record whether completed counts and visible cards agree across the three implementations.

Record state declarations, derived values, events, and the presence of explicit subscription cleanup in the comparison table. Separate preferences from observations. This example does not measure relative performance.
